item.title: Episode 15 / Everyday Mindfulness: PRESENCE — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Presence lets us override reactivity, putting values and intentional thought into the leadership position. Learn how.

item.title: Episode 16: Oxytocin & the Power of Love (Hormones) — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: What is this “love hormone” called Oxytocin? And what can we do to invite more of it into our lives?

item.title: Episode 17: The Body’s Way — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Nia founder Debbie Rosas shares the power and joy of of embodied movement.

item.title: Episode 18: Back to the Brain — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Dive in to the “body brain” here and tap into the under-celebrated superpowers of your FULL intelligence.

item.title: Episode 19: Breath and Presence with Zee Clarke — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Breath: the gift of life, the soul of many a practice, and a science/art that can change how we think and feel. Zee Clarke knows its power – and shares it here.

item.title: Episode 20: Inner Work, Outer Impact with Dr. Susanne von der Becke — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Dr. Susanne von der Becke sees a clear path to changing the world, one breath at a time: one that begins with you.

item.title: Episode 21: The BITCH is Back with Lucy Cooke — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Zooligist, bestselling author, and NatGeo Explorer Lucy Cooke tears through outdated stories about what it means to be female – and challenges the biases that might be holding a lot of us back.

item.title: Episode 22: More Than Skin Deep with Grace Gold — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: Beauty journalist, spokesperson, and all-around expert Grace Gold opens our eyes to new ways of looking at beauty, beyond the gaze of any products or campaigns telling us we need THEM to be our most radiant selves.

item.title: Episode 23: Getting Unstuck — The Brain and Beyond
item.description: A surprising look at what MIGHT be one cause of stuckness – and a possible brain “hack” that seems to have gotten me, for one, out of it.
